title: Heating curve of water
caption: Heating one mole of ice from −20 °C at a steady rate. The temperature stops rising while the ice melts (6.01 kJ) and while the water boils (40.7 kJ): the energy separates particles instead of speeding them up. Boiling takes far more energy because the molecules separate completely.
alt: Temperature against energy supplied: a short rise to 0 °C, a short flat stretch (melting), a rise to 100 °C, a long flat stretch (boiling), then a short rise.
description: Flat at 100 °C while boiling: 40.7 kJ, nearly seven times as long.

checks.name: the temperature is constant while water boils
liquid water reaches 100 °C after 18 g × 4.18 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ × 100 K = 7.52 kJ
boiling takes about 6.8 times the energy of melting (40.7 ÷ 6.01)
